stem: A company connects its on-premises data center to AWS over a single Direct Connect connection and wants an automatic path if that connection fails. Separately, its public-facing application serves users on several continents and needs each user's traffic to enter the AWS network at the location closest to them. Select TWO actions that address these two needs. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Create a VPC peering connection between the on-premises network and the VPC
Create a Transit Gateway peering connection to a Transit Gateway in another Region for on-premises resiliency
Configure a Site-to-Site VPN connection as an automatic backup path for the Direct Connect connection
Place a CloudFront distribution or Global Accelerator accelerator in front of the public-facing application
Route global user traffic through a NAT gateway to reach the application

rationale: A Site-to-Site VPN configured as a backup path takes over automatically if the Direct Connect connection fails, giving the on-premises link its resiliency. CloudFront or Global Accelerator gives global users a nearby AWS entry point, which is exactly what the second requirement asks for. VPC peering connects two VPCs' networks to each other; it has no mechanism to connect to an on-premises data center. Transit Gateway peering connects two Transit Gateways, typically across Regions, and has nothing to do with failing over an on-premises connection. A NAT gateway provides outbound internet access for private subnets; it does not bring inbound global user traffic in through a nearby edge location.
